entries.produces: Polynomial off-path Nashification given a suitable on-path state; strong hardness only of exact global lexmax; polynomial neighborhood search upper bound in PLS, not a full polynomial factor-two algorithm. Polynomial greedy transfer budgets alone, with a fixed-layout NE compatibility counterexample. New conditional bit-polynomial factor-two construction when greedy occupancy has uniform q>=2; conditional factor-three construction when greedy occupies k distinct sites; unopened-site cap invariant after site transfers. Wider componentwise equal-multiplicity factor-two subclass and a five-site frozen-site packing counterexample. Six-site strengthening proves global ordinary cap infeasible for one actual deviation despite a low-deviator exact NE. Initial greedy incidence ordering: each customer starts at a maximum-final-multiplicity accessible occupied site. New output-recognizable polynomial factor-two theorems for all-distinct greedy layouts and multiplicity-class range-certified layouts; the latter subsumes light-overlap and all-heavy-overlap conditions. Two exact integer examples refute arbitrary repair and heaviest-first repair while retaining an alternative good NE at the same greedy layout. New bit-polynomial factor-two construction for greedy occupied-overlap components of constant multiplicity or size at most two, including unequal multiplicities outside the range certificate. Two exact fixed-layout selection obstructions: unique bad lexmax customer assignment and unique bad global weighted-customer-potential minimizer. Arbitrary-size all-or-one mixed-multiplicity occupied components admit descending-weight minimum-normalized-load list assignment and bit-polynomial factor-two completion. A six-client strict-greedy three-site chain forces every downward-only client repair path to require an upward return. Nested-anchor partial overlaps with weight-ordered expanding eligible sets now admit restricted list assignment and full polynomial factor two; reversing sets refutes the unrestricted list rule only. Universal singleton reset from the original greedy assignment completes any supplied box-constrained on-path NE in polynomial time. A lower-bounded integral convex-cost flow constructs that box NE for arbitrary partial overlaps when all light multi-option clients have equal weight. A two-unequal-light-client parametric obstruction to lower-box-only weighted-potential minimization, with a box NE on the same layout. New bit-polynomial full factor-two construction for anchored light-star components with arbitrary unequal light weights and frozen heavy cross-component clients.
entries.limit: Historical source records only the arbitrary-k question, not these proofs. External priority/review unrecorded. STOC 2004 theorem imported only for restricted identical-link customer subgames. The reduction family has an easy exact SPE; PLS membership does not imply polynomial convergence. Neither restricted output class solves all-input unequal-multiplicity factor two; no canonical implementation yet. The stationary-site counterexample only invalidates a frozen-assignment packing interface, not factor-two existence. This cap obstruction does not prove the greedy layout or instance lacks a factor-two continuation. The newer distinct-site factor-two theorem supersedes the old factor-three guarantee for the same class. Range certification can fail on mixed-multiplicity inputs; neither counterexample shows greedy occupancy itself fails factor two. Mixed-q overlap components of three or more sites remain open. Both new selection obstructions are fixed-instance, site-pure/uniform on-path results; neither rules out another suitable on-path mixed NE or layout. The all-or-one condition excludes mixed-q partial-overlap components with three or more sites. The downward-only trap is a method obstruction with an exact NE after one return, not a factor-two lower bound. The nested-anchor condition includes genuine partial overlaps but excludes nonnested partial overlap; the reversed example has another exact NE and is not a greedy-layout counterexample. The general mixed-light-weight box-NE existence and polynomial selection question is open; the uniform-light example is a finite check, not a universal proof. This four-state family rejects only lower-constrained weighted-potential selection; it does not reject greedy box-NE existence or polynomial factor two. The anchored star condition is a sufficient restriction on light overlaps, not a theorem for arbitrary mixed-q partial overlap; the finite star audit checks only one instance.
